newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Ihlas Finans to revise targets.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Ihlas Finans to revise targets.

text.p: Turkey's Ihlas Finans Kurumu , the only financial institution listed on the Istanbul Exchange, will revise its 1996 forecasts after favourable results in the first eight months of the year, a senior company official said on Monday.

"After the increase in our deposits exceeded the 1996 target of 21 trillion lira in August, we decided to revise our deposit target for 1996. We should also revise our profit target as well," Ihlas general manager Mehmet Savas told Reuters.

Ihlas Finans Kurumu is 80-percent owned by Ihlas Holding A.S.. It began its Islamist banking operations -- based on profit sharing instead of interest earnings -- in April 1996 and opened a 15 percent of stake to the public on July 4.
The company initially targeted one trillion lira net profit and 21 trillion lira deposit. Savas said the two targets would be revised, but did not elaborate.
Ihlas officials say the company draws funds from those who avoid investing their savings in interest-bearing instruments because of religious concerns.
"We call deposits funds. We collect money from our customers and invest these funds in our projects or trading facilities. In return, we share profits or loss with our customers," Savas said.
Savas said the company's opening to the public was also a major factor behind its growth.
Ihlas' first-half net profit reached 240 billion lira and its deposits were 19.8 trillion lira after 166 billion lira and 9.2 trillion lira for the whole of 1995.
